decisions.reason: The index set is explicitly n>=1, so no cutoff at zero is used. The library's def-sequence Indexing remark explicitly permits sequences starting at 1 up to a shift; this definition is for real sequences, whereas the present vectors lie in H^(r). The cutoff bounds, weak product-domain memberships, dominated convergence and normalization of a nonzero tail prove exactly the asserted graph limits. The alleged indexing defect is false.

Step 2.1 incorrectly types a PVM on B(R^2) as the PVM of an assigned real-valued sharp observable. The already cited general-measurable-space probability lemma (b) supplies the required result, so this is a nonfatal application/citation defect. F1 and step 2.1 now explicitly apply that lemma with X=R^2. Step 1.1 also now derives rectangle products from PVM multiplicativity before invoking the joint criterion; the Statement and physical_scope are unchanged.

Original F3 invokes compatibility theorem (a) under P1/P2/P3 without adopting P1/P3, so its claimed citation is not licensed. Replaced the invocation by the local deduction H(Lambda x R)H(R x Sigma)=H(Lambda x Sigma)=H(R x Sigma)H(Lambda x R), using the already declared PVM definition. Translation covariance contradicts commutation on a nonzero Q-domain vector for t!=0; the no-joint-law conclusion retains exactly its original scope. Compatibility theorem now supplies vocabulary only, with formulation-prerequisite role.

Original F6 applies compatibility theorem (a) without P3, so the cited deduction is not licensed. Replaced it by PVM multiplicativity: any two marginals of one PVM must commute, contrary to the explicit i sigma_z/2 and cyclic projection witnesses. Added explicit AC/Countable Choice already declared in deps and required by spectral-atom, moment and Robertson suppliers. F4 now states exactly Cauchy-Schwarz; step 2.1 derives the vector integral norm bound locally by testing against M/|M|, handling M=0. Pointwise Bloch identity and integration allow spatial/internal entanglement, and the eigenstate product remains hbar^2/4.

F6 attributes general polynomial closure of Schwartz functions to a definition and a weak-derivative lemma that do not state it. This is a nonfatal local supplier-restatement defect. Removed the unsupported closure claim and distinguished smooth functions from L2 classes. Step 1.1 now derives each derivative as polynomial times the Gaussian and bounds every weighted monomial using the maximum of r^m exp(-cr^2); heat-kernel second moments give x_j psi in L2, hence the classical/weak derivative and maximal momentum-domain membership. Fourier coefficients, coordinate laws, spreads and linear-first imaginary pairing are unchanged and correct.

The supplier is explicitly kind counterexample and its interface heading is Statement refuted, not Statement. Its construction takes periodic/antiperiodic momentum extensions agreeing on the dense invariant test-function domain, but the spectral projections onto 1 and exp(i pi x) fail to commute: on 1 the two products give 4/pi^2 and (-2i/pi) exp(i pi x). Therefore the remark faithfully says the displayed implication is refuted. No graph-norm core claim is made. The inventory/model/empirical-scope prose is also faithful, and the changed spin supplier remains a conditional model deduction under its explicit choice assumptions.
